hints: Look closely at where each number sits: in the root is it in the central star or between its arms, in the stem is it on the outer or inner side of the bundle, and in the leaf is it above or below the midrib bundle?
Remember the position rule: phloem lies between the arms of xylem in the root, on the outside of xylem in a stem vascular bundle, and below (abaxial to) xylem in the leaf midrib.
walkthrough:
**Start with the root**

Look at the centre of the root. Label 1 is the large four-armed star in the middle. That is xylem. Label 2 is the small patches sitting between the xylem arms. Those outer patches are phloem. So for root, phloem is 2.

**Move to the stem bundle**

In a young dicot stem, each vascular bundle has phloem on the outside (towards the epidermis) and xylem on the inside (towards the pith). Label 3 is the outer part of the bundle, so it is phloem. Label 4 is the inner part, so it is xylem. So for stem, phloem is 3.

**Finish with the leaf midrib**

In the leaf midrib, xylem is uppermost (adaxial, facing the palisade mesophyll for water supply) and phloem is lowermost (abaxial). Label 5 is the top half of the midrib bundle, so xylem. Label 6 is the bottom half, so phloem. So for leaf, phloem is 6.

**Put it together**

Phloem is 2 in root, 3 in stem, 6 in leaf. That matches row C exactly.

options.A: Incorrect because 1 is xylem in the root centre, not phloem, and 5 is xylem in the upper leaf midrib, not phloem.
options.B: Incorrect because 1 is root xylem and 4 is stem xylem on the inner side of the bundle, although 6 is correctly leaf phloem.
options.C: Correct because 2 is phloem between root xylem arms, 3 is phloem on the outer side of the stem bundle, and 6 is phloem below xylem in the leaf.
options.D: Incorrect because 4 is stem xylem and 5 is leaf xylem, although 2 is correctly root phloem.
